enhanced_information: Factor V Leiden is a genetic mutation that leads to resistance to activated protein C, not protein S, and is not associated with anticardiolipin antibodies or acquired disorders. It does not cause a prolongation of the partial thromboplastin time (PTT), as PTT remains normal. Factor V Leiden, along with the prothrombin mutation, is one of the most common genetic-based thrombotic predispositions. Therefore, the correct statement is that Factor V Leiden, together with the prothrombin mutation, constitutes the most frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition in our environment.
analysis: Factor V Leiden is a genetic mutation that leads to resistance to activated protein C, not protein S. It is not an acquired disorder and is not associated with anticardiolipin antibodies, which are related to antiphospholipid syndrome. The presence of Factor V Leiden does not cause a prolongation of the partial thromboplastin time. The mutation is indeed one of the most common genetic predispositions to thrombosis, along with the prothrombin mutation. Therefore, the statement that Factor V Leiden, together with the prothrombin mutation, constitutes the most frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition is true.
